findings.source_passage: feeling a great deal worse than I have ever done since, even from the greatest subsequent misfortunes
findings.source_locator: third paragraph, near end of childhood-memory sequence
findings.why_it_matters: The phrase 'even from the greatest subsequent misfortunes' is a characteristic Ishmael aside that casts an ironic shadow over all his later trials, including the Pequod's fate; its omission removes interpretive resonance.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'even from the greatest subsequent misfortunes' after 'feeling worse than I have ever done since.'

findings.source_passage: if he had not been a small degree civilized, he very probably would not have troubled himself with boots at all; but then, if he had not been still a savage, he never would have dreamt of getting under the bed to put them on
findings.source_locator: fifth paragraph, 'neither caterpillar nor butterfly' passage
findings.why_it_matters: This is the logical punch-line of the 'undergraduate / transition stage' conceit—the rhetorical structure that makes Melville's civilisation-versus-savagery joke land. Without it, the caterpillar/butterfly metaphor hangs unresolved.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the two-clause sentence beginning 'If he had not been a small degree civilized…' immediately after 'He was an undergraduate.'

findings.source_passage: no two parts of which were of one precise shade—owing I suppose to his keeping his arm at sea unmethodically in sun and shade, his shirt sleeves irregularly rolled up at various times
findings.source_locator: first paragraph, describing the tattooed arm
findings.why_it_matters: The parenthetical explanation is a characteristic Ishmaelian pseudo-scientific aside that establishes the narrator's observational voice; its removal slightly flattens the quilt-arm comparison.
findings.suggested_fix: Reinsert the explanatory clause about sun and shade after 'Cretan labyrinth of a figure' to preserve the narrator's digressive voice.

findings.source_passage: and the sound of gay voices all over the house
findings.source_locator: third paragraph, describing what Ishmael hears while confined to bed
findings.why_it_matters: The detail completes the sensory trio (light, coaches, voices) that intensifies the child's misery; its omission mildly weakens the accumulative effect.
findings.suggested_fix: Add 'and the sound of gay voices all over the house' after 'a great rattling of coaches in the streets.'

findings.source_passage: Afterwards I wondered the less at this operation when I came to know of what fine steel the head of a harpoon is made, and how exceedingly sharp the long straight edges are always kept
findings.source_locator: sixth paragraph, after the harpoon-shaving scene
findings.why_it_matters: The retrospective rationalisation is a small but voice-typical Ishmael coda that links the comic scene to the novel's larger world of whaling craft; its loss is minor but noticeable.
findings.suggested_fix: Append the sentence beginning 'Afterwards I wondered the less…' after 'Rogers's best cutlery with a vengeance.'

summary: The draft preserves all high-priority verbatim passages faithfully but drops two medium-weight voice-establishing elaborations (the 'greatest subsequent misfortunes' aside and the boots-civilisation punchline) and three minor Ishmaelian digressions, none severe enough individually to require regeneration.
